newsitem.title: DENMARK: POLL - SAS SEEN BACK IN BLACK IN H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: POLL - SAS SEEN BACK IN BLACK IN H1 1997.

text.p: Seven analysts polled by Reuters on Tuesday forecast that Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) would swing back into surplus in 1997's second quarter but that the six-month profit would be almost half that of 1996.

The panel predicted that SAS' second quarter pre-tax profit would be an average 863 million Swedish crowns, more or less unchanged from the same 1996 period's 865 million crowns, but considerably better than 1997's first quarter loss of 269 million Swedish crowns.
The estimates for the second quarter lay within the 649 million to 1.021 billion Swedish crown range.

For the first half of 1997, the analysts forecast an average pre-tax profit of 594 million Swedish crowns, with estimates between 380-752 million crowns, against a 1.176 billion Swedish crown pre-tax surplus in 1996's first six months.
SAS is due to announce its interim 1997 results on August 13.
